title: A reset or reused reader wrapper keeps its original owner's binding, so taint leaks across owners
claim: The reader binding is keyed on the wrapper address and set once at construction. bufio.Reader.Reset and LimitedReader.R reassignment are unhooked, so a later io.ReadAll on the wrapper adopts new clean data or another request's data as the original owner's http.request.body source. That causes in-request false positives and cross-owner attribution for pooled bufio readers.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -count=1 -v -run TestReview ./iast/io/ (with .omo/review/evidence/hooks-io-bufio/zz_review_repro_test.go copied into iast/io)

title: A MultiReader with any bound input taints the whole ReadAll result, including clean and other-owner data
claim: The result is bound if any of the first 8 inputs is bound, and ReadAll adopts the whole result as a single body source. Clean readers are tainted, the source value contains non-request bytes, and a bound but empty body makes a fully clean result tainted. The existing test enshrines the merged 'included-excluded' source value.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -count=1 -v -run TestReviewMultiReaderCleanPrefixTainted ./iast/io/

title: Common body-reading idioms silently lose provenance
claim: Pooled bufio readers initialized through Reset, io.NopCloser value wrappers, the bytes.NewReader body-restore idiom, and bufio ReadString/ReadBytes/Scanner results are untainted. These are safe misses, but the README does not document them.

title: Reader hooks run on every process-wide call while any analysis is active
claim: The only gate is manager.used==0. While any request is sampled, every wrapper and ReadAll call in the process pays for reflect.ValueOf plus a 64-owner TryRLock scan, and a MultiReader pays up to 8 times. A live reader-binding counter would make the gate cheap.
